texts.common.a_saved_data_file_is_identified: a saved-data file is identified by its extension, .sav.
texts.error.boot_rom: The boot ROM %1 is missing or is not %2 bytes. Give it, or set Boot ROM to off.
texts.error.no_file: No game file is in the project.
texts.error.not_loaded: '%1' could not be loaded: Gearboy does not know its kind of cartridge.
texts.error.not_read: The game '%1' could not be read.
texts.error.sgb_cartridge: %1 is not a Super Game Boy cartridge that Gearboy knows. It knows three dumps of the Super Game Boy's cartridge and one of the Super Game Boy 2's.
texts.error.sgb_missing: The Super Game Boy cartridge %1 is missing. Give it, or set Super Game Boy cartridge to none.
texts.error.too_short: '%1' is too short to be a Game Boy game (%2 bytes).
texts.firmware.cgb_boot_bin.about: The Game Boy Color's boot ROM (CGB), 2,304 bytes. It is Nintendo's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.dmg_boot_bin.about: The Game Boy's boot ROM (DMG), 256 bytes. It is Nintendo's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.sgb1_sfc.about: The Super Game Boy's own cartridge, a Super Nintendo game of 256 KB. Gearboy takes the Super Game Boy's border and colours from it. It is Nintendo's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.sgb2_sfc.about: The Super Game Boy 2's own cartridge, a Super Nintendo game of 512 KB. Gearboy takes the Super Game Boy's border and colours from it. It is Nintendo's and you have to supply it.
texts.setting.bootrom.about: 'on' starts the console with its own start-up program, the boot ROM, which shows the logo before the game starts; you have to supply it. 'off' starts the game at once, in the state the boot ROM would have left the console in. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.colorcorrection.about: 'on' changes the Game Boy Color's colours to look more like its screen did. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.model.about: Which console the game runs on: GB the Game Boy, GBC the Game Boy Color, GBA a Game Boy Advance running a Game Boy Color game (a few games add things on it), and SGB the Super Game Boy on a Super Nintendo, which puts the game's border around the picture and takes up to four controllers. Gearboy runs a Game Boy game on the Game Boy Color as on a Game Boy, without the colours a Game Boy Color gives it. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.palette.about: The four shades of a Game Boy game's picture: Gearboy's green, or greys. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.sgbcartridge.about: The Super Game Boy's own cartridge, which you have to supply: SGB1 the Super Game Boy's, SGB2 the Super Game Boy 2's. With it, the picture has the Super Game Boy's border and colours before a game sends its own, and a game made only for the Game Boy runs in the border too. With none, a game made for the Super Game Boy draws its own border and colours, and any other game runs as on a Game Boy. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.slot.game.help: The Game Boy or Game Boy Color game: the cartridge's contents, a .gb or .gbc file (.sgb for a Super Game Boy one).
texts.slot.savedata.help: The cartridge's battery-backed memory at the start, for a project that begins from a saved game: a file as Emulator > Export Save Data... writes it, or a .sav file of Gearboy's or of another emulator. The file is never changed. Leave this empty to start with the cartridge's memory empty.
